title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000031: the void*-declared database and OS-queue APIs are correctly polymorphic, so the pointer-identity test failure is a test-harness assertion defect, not a product API defect
lifecycle_status_note: 'draft': this record states a measured root cause and a demonstrated, but only partially applied, test-side remediation. One of the affected tests is fixed and green; the remaining affected tests are NOT fixed. No human reviewer has confirmed the analysis, and human approval remains 'pending'. This record makes no MISRA conformance claim, no tool-qualification claim and no certification claim of any kind.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: First record of this defect. Re-derives the call-site map from source, establishes that the void* parameters are required by design, refutes the proposed product-side fix with a measured type census, and demonstrates the correct test-side fix on one representative test with a non-vacuity check.

evidence: CALL-SITE MAP, re-derived from source (the reported line numbers were verified, not trusted). Affected declarations: src/app/engine/database/database.h declares DATA_Write1/2/3/4DataBlocks and DATA_Read1/2/3/4DataBlocks with untyped void* parameters; src/app/task/os/os.h:389,402 declares OS_ReceiveFromQueue(OS_QUEUE, void *const pvBuffer, uint32_t) and OS_SendToBackOfQueue(OS_QUEUE, const void *const pvItemToQueue, uint32_t). The product-side callers do not call these functions directly. They go through the variadic macros DATA_WRITE_DATA(...) and DATA_READ_DATA(...) defined at database.h:84-102, which expand to the arity-selected DATA_*DataBlocks function. Measured caller counts: DATA_WRITE_DATA 72 call sites in src/*.c plus 4 in src/*.h; DATA_READ_DATA 68 in src/*.c plus 4 in src/*.h; OS_ReceiveFromQueue 14 src/*.c call sites; OS_SendToBackOfQueue 17 src/*.c call sites. 142 DATA_* macro invocations were resolved to their argument types. WHAT THE FUNCTIONS ACTUALLY WRITE, read from the implementation and not the comment: DATA_CopyData (database.c:164-196) does a raw memcpy of a runtime-determined dataLength into or out of a byte array. That length is obtained in DATA_IterateOverDatabaseEntries (database.c:220) from data_baseHeader.pDatabase[entryIndex].dataLength, where entryIndex is derived by reading the uniqueId field out of the caller's own struct (database.c:213-216). So neither the pointee type nor the copy length is a property of the function signature; both are properties of the value the caller passes. TYPES VARY BY CALL SITE, decisively: 34 of the 37 DATA_BLOCK_*_s types defined in src/ (91% of the database) are provably passed at DATA_WRITE_DATA/DATA_READ_DATA call sites, including DATA_BLOCK_CELL_VOLTAGE_s, DATA_BLOCK_SOC_s, DATA_BLOCK_SOH_s, DATA_BLOCK_POWER_s, DATA_BLOCK_STATE_REQUEST_s and 28 others. OS_ReceiveFromQueue and OS_SendToBackOfQueue receive 10 and 11 distinct buffer expressions respectively, resolving to at least DATA_QUEUE_MESSAGE_s, CAN_MESSAGE_t, the N77X I2C transaction struct, ADI_REQUEST_s, the RTC time struct, a uint8_t element of a receive array, and a socket-descriptor int. Both are one-line wrappers over FreeRTOS xQueueReceive and xQueueSendToBack (os_freertos.c:293-316), whose own public API is void*-based and whose item size is fixed at queue-creation time. THE FAILURE MECHANISM, read from the CMock 2.7.2 generator source rather than inferred: conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml:368-369 sets :memcmp_if_unknown: true and :when_ptr: :compare_data but loads only the :callback and :return_thru_ptr plugins, so CMock's array handling is off. cmock_generator_utils.rb:207-210 then selects UNITY_TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_PTR for any void* argument, with the in-source comment 'void* cannot be safely dereferenced; without the array plugin there is no way to specify depth, so fall back to comparing the pointer value itself'. The resulting assertion is pointer identity, which cannot hold, because the test and the code under test each hold their own file-scope static copy with internal linkage. Observed verbatim for the five originally-known sites: test_diag_cfg.c 'Expected 0x0000000100840000 Was 0x0000000100840098:Function DATA_Write4DataBlocks Argument pDataFromSender0', test_moving_average.c:135, test_soc_lookup-table.c:114, test_state_estimation.c:116/123/129/135, all of the same form. NO CMock CONFIGURATION CAN SIZE A void* PARAMETER: cmock_header_parser.rb:519-520 applies :treat_as_array only when the argument is NOT a pointer, so it cannot supply a pointee size for void*; and :treat_as_void widens the set of types routed into the identity branch rather than sizing them. The only other void* branch, cmock_generator_utils.rb:211-215, requires the array plugin and then hardcodes depth 1, which would compare a single byte and would be a weakened assertion. THE PRODUCT CODE IS CORRECT, demonstrated rather than argued: replacing the unsatisfiable identity expectation in tests/unit/app/engine/config/test_diag_cfg.c with a CMock callback that does TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_MEMORY over sizeof(DATA_BLOCK_ERROR_STATE_s), sizeof(DATA_BLOCK_MOL_FLAG_s), sizeof(DATA_BLOCK_RSL_FLAG_s) and sizeof(DATA_BLOCK_MSL_FLAG_s) makes that test pass, with no change to any file under src/. The oracle was then shown to be non-vacuous: deliberately setting .aerosolAlert = true in the test's own copy of DATA_BLOCK_ERROR_STATE_s makes it fail with 'Memory Mismatch. Byte 70 Expected 0x01 Was 0x00:Function DATA_Write4DataBlocks', after which the deliberate change was reverted.
impact: The reported framing, that this is a product API defect, is incorrect, and acting on it would cause harm. Typing these parameters is not merely inelegant, it is impossible to do correctly: a single concrete type would be wrong for at least 33 of the 37 database entry types, so the change would either break the build on const conversions at the ~146 product call sites or silently mistype most of the database. A reviewer who 'fixed' the signature would be making a safety-relevant data path less safe while believing they were improving it. What the defect actually costs is verification coverage, not product integrity: 17 tests and 36 assertions currently carry an assertion that can never pass, so those code paths have no working oracle. 14 of those tests remain red after this change, so the coverage gap is only partly closed. It is worth stating the limit of what was demonstrated: the callback fix was applied and verified on one test, test_diag_cfg.c, chosen as the cleanest case with a single expectation on a single function. It has NOT been applied to the other 14 affected tests, several of which interleave expectations on two or three different mocked functions and depend on return values that vary per call, so a per-test callback there is a redesign of the test rather than a mechanical edit, and doing it blind risks introducing real regressions in tests that are the project's only oracle. The two independent defects previously reported alongside this one are unaffected by this work and remain open: the CMock compare_data-on-a-by-value-uint64_t configuration defect at src/app/driver/can/cbs/can_helper.h:131, which is a conf/unit defect and not a product defect, and the un-isolated test_dp83869.c segfault. Nothing here is evidence of MISRA conformance, of tool qualification, or of any certification, and no such claim may be inferred from this record.
root_cause: The product declarations are correct and the test-side expectation mechanism is wrong. Three independent conditions combine. First, the APIs are genuinely polymorphic and their void* is required: the database access functions derive both the pointee type and the copy length at run time from a uniqueId field read out of the caller's own struct (database.c:213-222), and the OS queue wrappers are thin pass-throughs to FreeRTOS whose queue item type is fixed at creation time. The project has already documented this intent itself: src/app/engine/database/database.c:177 carries an active upstream MISRA/Axivion suppression reading 'AXIVION Next Codeline Style MisraC2012-11.5 this casted is required in order to have a generic interface for all database entries'. Second, conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml asks CMock to compare pointers by content (:when_ptr: :compare_data) while providing CMock no way to learn the pointee size of a void* and not loading the plugin that would allow a depth to be specified, so the generator silently falls back to pointer identity. Third, the tests register their expectation against their own file-scope static copy of the data block while the code under test passes its own different static copy, so identity can never hold. The tests are not wrong in intent: the test author's own comment reads '/** local copy of the #DATA_BLOCK_ERROR_STATE_s table */', which shows a content comparison was intended. A content assertion was silently downgraded into an identity assertion by the configuration, and that downgrade is invisible in the test source.
resolution: PARTIALLY RESOLVED, and deliberately so. Resolved: the test-side assertion mechanism for one representative test, tests/unit/app/engine/config/test_diag_cfg.c, now performs the full-struct content comparison its author intended, via a CMock callback using the :callback plugin the project already loads; the test is green and its oracle was proven non-vacuous. Verified by a full 313-test host sweep executed before and after the change, from identical 313-test result sets: 195 pass / 18 fail / 100 build failures before, 196 pass / 17 fail / 100 after, 877 assertions tested in both, assertions passing 819 to 820, assertions failing 55 to 54, with exactly one outcome change in the whole suite and zero regressions, and with all build-failure classifications unchanged. Also resolved: the undocumented polymorphism is now stated in the Doxygen of all four affected database functions and both affected OS queue functions in database.h and os.h, so the reason the pointer cannot be typed is legible to the next maintainer at the point of the declaration. That documentation change is comment-only; every changed line in src/ is a Doxygen line and no executable line was touched, so it cannot alter behaviour. Explicitly NOT done, and recommended against: the proposed product-side fix of typing the parameters. It is rejected on the evidence above, not on judgement. NOT done: the same callback treatment for the remaining 14 affected tests, which is a test-ownership decision rather than a mechanical change and carries real regression risk against the project's only oracle; the verified recipe is the one applied to test_diag_cfg.c. Still open and out of scope here: the conf/unit CMock compare_data-on-a-by-value-scalar defect at can_helper.h:131, whose correct fix is a :treat_as entry for uint64 or :memcmp_if_unknown: false, both of which are changes to conf/ that this task was not authorised to make; and the un-isolated test_dp83869.c segfault, which was not investigated and remains as previously reported.
